findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Matrix/Mul.lean:381 `theorem diagonal_mul_diagonal (d₁ d₂ : n → α) : diagonal d₁ * diagonal d₂ = diagonal (d₁ * d₂)` — and it is the lemma used in this proof (DiagonalCosets.lean:95).
findings.issue: `natDiagGL_mul` states `natDiagGL a * natDiagGL b = natDiagGL (a * b)`, but the `f_mul` pattern (`Nat.cast_mul`, `map_mul`) means `f (a * b) = f a * f b`, i.e. the name advertises the reverse orientation. Mathlib's name for this exact shape is `diagonal_mul_diagonal`.

findings.evidence: Statement at CoprimeMul.lean:309-310; listed under `## Main results` at line 38. Contrast in-file neighbours that do name their subject (`natDiagGL_mem_posDetInt`, DiagonalCosets.lean:104).
findings.fix: Rename to name the actual left-hand side, e.g. `natDiagGL_mul_mapGL_mul_natDiagGL_mem_doubleCoset_of_coprime`.
findings.issue: `mul_mem_doubleCoset_of_coprime` is a public main result whose name reads as "a product lies in the double coset", i.e. a closure property of `doubleCoset` under multiplication. Nothing in the name identifies the subject `natDiagGL n a * mapGL ℚ τ * natDiagGL n b`.

findings.evidence: `private def congMod` at CongruenceSplit.lean:44; public `lemma exists_mul_congMod_of_coprime` at line 137 with the divisibility written out at lines 140-141.
findings.fix: Either make the predicate part of the public API (and state the lemma in terms of it), or name the lemma after what it actually says, e.g. `exists_mul_dvd_sub_one_of_coprime`.
findings.issue: The public `exists_mul_congMod_of_coprime` is named after `congMod`, which is a `private def` (line 44) and does not appear in the statement — the statement spells out `(d : ℤ) ∣ (τ₁ i j - if i = j then 1 else 0)`. A user cannot resolve the `congMod` component of the name.

findings.evidence: CoprimeMul.lean:504 and 535 conclude `∈ SLnZ n`; sibling helpers `conjugate_congruent_mem_SLnZ` (226), `inv_conjugate_congruent_mem_SLnZ` (261), `mem_SLnZ_of_coprime_scaling` (374). `_mem_H` is only otherwise used in Commutativity.lean, where `H : Subgroup G` is an actual variable.
findings.issue: `coprime_coupling_mem_H` and `out_conj_diagA_mem_H` (line 526) conclude `∈ SLnZ n`, but name the group `H`, which is not bound anywhere in this file; `diagA` likewise names no declaration (it is the local `δa`). Neighbours in the same file use `_mem_SLnZ`.

`natDiagGL_const_conj_eq` (66), `conjAct_natDiagGL_const_smul_eq` (72) and `conjAct_rep_diagCoset_const_smul_eq` (93) end in a bare `_eq` that names no right-hand side; all three conclude `= <the argument itself>`. Mathlib's name for exactly this shape is `_eq_self`, and that very lemma is used in the proof at line 101.

findings.evidence: No `CRT` in any Mathlib declaration name; `chineseRemainder` at mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Nat/ModEq.lean:464 and mathlib/Mathlib/Data/ZMod/Basic.lean:885. Public downstream lemma is `exists_mul_congMod_of_coprime` (line 137).
findings.fix: Rename to the `exists_mul_congMod_*` family, e.g. `exists_mul_congMod_of_coprime_transvection` and `exists_mul_congMod_mul`.
findings.issue: `transvection_CRT` and `crtProd_mul` (123) use the acronym `CRT`/`crt`, which appears in no Mathlib declaration name; the standard term is `chineseRemainder`. `crtProd` also names no declaration, and `transvection_CRT` proves an existence statement without the `exists_` prefix its own downstream lemma uses.

findings.evidence: Statements at CoprimeMul.lean:412-414 and 438-440; naming-conventions rule "`_`-separated strings in a lemma name correspond to a definition name or connective".
findings.fix: Rename after the conclusion, e.g. `exists_intCast_eq_prod_mul_natDiagGL_conj_apply` and `exists_intCast_eq_prod_mul_natDiagGL_sandwich_apply`.
findings.issue: `diagConj_scaling` and `diagSandwich_scaling` (436) describe the proof idea rather than the conclusion, which is `∃ z : ℤ, (∏ k, (a k : ℚ)) * C i j = z` — an integrality statement. `diagConj` and `diagSandwich` also correspond to no declaration, contrary to the rule that `_`-separated components match a definition name or connective.

summary: Several introduced names misdescribe their statements: `natDiagGL_mul` advertises the opposite orientation from Mathlib's `diagonal_mul_diagonal` precedent, `mul_mem_doubleCoset_of_coprime` reads as a closure property, a public lemma is named after a private predicate, and helper names use an undefined `H` and a non-Mathlib `CRT` acronym.
